grammar_focus: It was … that 强调句(强调状语)、neither … nor(既不…也不…)、be to do(表‘要/将/注定’)、by + 动名词(通过做…,表方式)、so … that(如此…以致…)(NCE4 该课源无独立 KS 页,考点由课文结构自取;IP:源为 H.H. Swinnerton《The Earth beneath Us》一段讲地震仪原理的科普文,系版权作品——已用 100% 原创行文复述其原理、无引用原句;题材=地震物理·无害;美语化 program/catalog;第四册第42课)
scene: 地震像夜里的窃贼,毫无预警地到来。因此,人们必须发明既不打盹、也不睡觉的仪器。最早的一些装置相当简单。比如有一种,是把粗细、长短不一的小木杆像九柱戏的木柱那样,竖立在一张坚硬的桌子上。当震动传来、摇动桌子时,轻微的震颤只会推倒最不稳的木杆,而剧烈的震颤则把它们全都掀倒。于是这些木杆,借着倒下、以及倒下的方向,替熟睡的科学家记录下了两件事:一次连他都没能惊醒的微弱震动的强度,以及它来自的方向。但若要取得真正重大的进展,就需要精密得多的仪器。所追求的理想,是一种能用笔在纸上记录地震经过时地面运动的装置。我写字时,笔在动而纸不动;只要多加练习,我迟早也能学会让笔不动、纸动着来写字。这听上去像个荒唐的主意,却正是早期地震仪所采用的原理。难处在于:当桌子、笔架和纸一起晃动时,怎样才能写得清楚?关键藏在一个日常观察里。一位站着的乘客,为什么在公交车骤然起步时容易向后倒?因为他的脚随车前移,而他的头一瞬间却还留在原处。把一个重物拴在一根长绳末端,握住绳子让重物几乎触到地面;这时把手来回晃动,你会发现重物只是轻微地动,甚至几乎不动。最早的仪器正是依据这一原理造出来的:悬着的重物和它带的笔保持不动,而纸在笔尖下面来回移动,于是纸的每一点动作都被墨水描了下来。在最早的仪器里,纸绕在一只缓缓转动的圆筒上;当圆筒被轻轻摇动时,笔画出的线便左右扭动。然而这样的图示记录,只反映了运动中水平的那一部分,而实际的运动要复杂得多。现代仪器可以如此安放,使上下、前后、左右三种运动各自被记录在不同的图表上。当仪器距地震中心超过七百英里时,记录会显示三道波以短暂的间隔一道接一道地到来。第一道标志着较快的纵波的到达;第二道是较慢的横波,晚几分钟才到。正是从对这两道——都穿过地球本体而行——的耐心研究中,人们才对地球隐秘的内部了解了如此之多。

grammar_card.title: It was … that 强调句 / neither … nor / be to do / by + 动名词 / so … that
grammar_card.intro: ①It is/was + 被强调部分 + that + 其余:强调状语等成分。②neither … nor …:‘既不…也不…’。③be to do:表‘要/将/注定/职责’(if any advance was to be made)。④by + 动名词:‘通过做…’,表方式。⑤so + 形容词/副词 + that …:‘如此…以致…’。

specialRules.rule: 强调句 It is/was … that …:去掉 It is/was 和 that 后,句子仍成立;强调人时 that 可换 who。
neither … nor 连接两项,谓语常就近一致;be to do 表按计划、职责或注定要发生的事。
美式拼写:program(程序,英式 programme)、catalog(目录,英式 catalogue)。本课已按美语写。

prelisten.q: Listen and answer — What does a pen have to do to record on paper the vibrations generated by an earthquake?
options: It must stay still while the paper moves beneath it, so its point traces the movement
It must move up and down very fast
It must be pressed hard onto the drum
It must be replaced after every shock

passage: An earthquake comes like a thief in the night, without warning. It was necessary, therefore, to invent instruments that neither slumbered nor slept. Some of the earliest devices were quite simple. One, for instance, consisted of rods of various lengths and thicknesses which stood on end like ninepins on a rigid table. When a shock came and shook the table, a gentle tremor toppled only the least stable rods, while a violent one brought them all down. Thus the rods, by falling and by the direction in which they fell, recorded for the sleeping scientist both the strength of a shock too weak to wake him and the direction from which it had come. But instruments far more delicate than these were needed if any really serious advance was to be made. The ideal to be aimed at was a device that could record, with a pen on paper, the movements of the ground as the quake passed by. While I write, my pen moves but the paper keeps still; with practice, I could in time learn to write by holding the pen still while the paper moved. That sounds a silly idea, yet it was precisely the principle adopted in the early seismometers. The difficulty is this: when table, penholder and paper are all shaking together, how is it possible to write legibly? The key lay in an everyday observation. Why does a standing passenger tend to fall when a bus starts suddenly? Because his feet move on with the bus, but his head, for an instant, stays still. Tie a heavy weight to a long string and hold it so that the weight nearly touches the ground; now move your hand to and fro, and it will be found that the weight moves only slightly, or not at all. It was upon this principle that the first instruments were made: the suspended weight and its pen stayed still, while the paper moved from side to side beneath the pen point, so that its every motion was traced in ink. In the first instruments the paper was wound round a slowly turning drum, and while the drum was gently shaken, the line the pen was drawing wriggled from side to side. Such a graphic record, however, shows only the horizontal part of the movement, which is in fact far more complicated. Modern instruments can be so placed that the up-and-down, to-and-fro and side-to-side motions are each set down in separate graphs. When the instrument is more than seven hundred miles from the earthquake's centre, the record shows three waves arriving one after another at short intervals. The first marks the arrival of the faster, longitudinal vibrations; the second, the slower, transverse vibrations, which arrive several minutes later. It was from the patient study of these two, both of which travel through the body of the earth, that so much was learned about the planet's hidden interior.

stage5.stem: "It was upon this principle ___ the first seismometers were made."(强调句 It was … 后接的那个连接词)
stage5.stem_cn: 正是依据这一原理,最早的地震仪被制造出来。

stage5.stem: "It was from these two waves ___ scientists learned about the earth's interior."(强调句 It was … 后接的那个连接词)
stage5.stem_cn: 正是从这两种波中,科学家了解了地球内部。

stage5.stem: "It ___ in the dead of night that the earthquake struck the sleeping city."(强调句,填 be 动词的过去式)
stage5.stem_cn: 正是在深夜,地震袭击了沉睡的城市。

stage5.stem: "The instrument must be one that neither slumbers ___ sleeps."(‘既不…也不…’,填第二个连词)
stage5.stem_cn: 这仪器必须既不打盹也不睡觉。

stage5.stem: "___ the table nor the paper stays perfectly still during a quake."(‘既不…也不…’,填第一个连词)
stage5.stem_cn: 地震时桌子和纸都不会完全静止。

stage5.stem: "A good record shows neither too little ___ too much movement."(‘既不…也不…’,填第二个连词)
stage5.stem_cn: 好的记录显示的运动既不太少也不太多。

stage5.stem: "If any serious advance ___ to be made, finer instruments were needed."(be to do 表‘要/将’,填 be 动词过去式)
stage5.stem_cn: 若要取得真正重大的进展,就需要更精密的仪器。

stage5.stem: "The ideal ___ be aimed at was a pen that wrote by itself."(不定式被动作定语,填该不定式最前面的记号)
stage5.stem_cn: 所追求的理想,是一支能自己书写的笔。

stage5.stem: "The scientists knew the great wave ___ to arrive last of all."(be to do 表‘注定/将’,填 be 动词过去式)
stage5.stem_cn: 科学家知道那道巨波注定最后才到。

stage5.stem: "The rods, ___ falling, recorded the strength and direction of the shock."(‘通过做…’表方式,填那个介词)
stage5.stem_cn: 那些木杆通过倒下,记录了震动的强度和方向。

stage5.stem: "One could learn to write by ___ the pen still while the paper moved."(by + 动名词,填‘保持’那个动词的动名词)
stage5.stem_cn: 人可以通过让笔不动、纸移动来学写字。

stage5.stem: "The seismometer records the quake by ___ the paper move under a still pen."(by + 动名词,填‘让’那个动词的动名词)
stage5.stem_cn: 地震仪通过让纸在静止的笔下移动来记录地震。

stage5.stem: "The instruments can be ___ placed that all three elements are recorded."(‘如此…以致…’结构,填第一个词)
stage5.stem_cn: 仪器可以如此安放,以致三种成分都被记录下来。

stage5.stem: "The shock was ___ gentle that only the loosest rods fell."(‘如此…以致…’,填第一个词)
stage5.stem_cn: 那次震动如此轻微,以致只有最松的木杆倒下。

stage5.stem: "The pen moved ___ little that the line was almost straight."(‘如此…以致…’,填第一个词)
stage5.stem_cn: 笔动得如此之小,以致画出的线几乎是直的。

stage5.stem: "A sudden violent shaking of the ground is an ___."(“地震”用哪个词)
"Something stiff and not able to bend is ___."(“坚硬的,僵直的”用哪个词)
"To twist and turn the body with small quick movements is to ___."(“扭动,蠕动”用哪个词)
stage5.stem_cn: 身体以细小快速的动作扭来扭去。
